placement.position_note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-0078). This building does not stand centred on a lot at a typology setback: it stands ON the north face of blk_randolph_dearborn, the block's Randolph Street frontage, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is 1.50 m back from that lot line, which is the closest line the plat module's own margin allows and is not a measurement of this frontage, and its west wall is fixed by the west end of the run's own frontage, 1.5 m clear of the side lot line at that end. The bearing is the face's own, so the front looks square at Randolph Street. The run carries no lateral offset, because a shared party wall is one wall and cannot wander. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, which building it was, and that these particular units stood shoulder to shoulder. What the 1834 South Water Street view supports is the TREATMENT — a continuous working row of party walls rather than detached cottages set back on grass. The treatment is what this placement takes from it, and a run standing on any other face of the town is borrowing it from that one street: the view draws a row, it does not place this row. Standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot, and the side lot lines this row crosses were always conjectural.

persons.name: Elijah Kent Hubbard
persons.note: THE 1835 POLL LIST AND A SECOND INDEPENDENT SOURCE. Read from death_notice, newspaper_1833_1835, poll_1835. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1a), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 26 times, as “HUBBARD ELIJAH K”, “HUBBARD E K”, 1835-06-26 to 1836-06-28: 24 federal land entries — E2NE sec 22 T38N R14E; E2NW sec 14 T39N R13E; E2NW sec 18 T38N R14E; E2NW sec 21 T38N R14E; E2NW sec 32 T41N R14E; E2SE sec 23 T38N R14E; E2SE sec 31 T38N R15E; N2 sec 08 T39N R13E; NEFR sec 32 T41N R14E; SE sec 26 T38N R14E; SE sec 36 T38N R14E; SW sec 08 T39N R13E; SW sec 27 T38N R14E; W2NE sec 18 T38N R14E; W2NE sec 20 T38N R14E; W2NE sec 22 T38N R14E; W2NE sec 24 T38N R14E; W2NE sec 26 T38N R14E; W2NW sec 21 T38N R14E; W2NW sec 31 T38N R15E; W2SE sec 08 T39N R13E; W2SE sec 24 T38N R14E; W2SE sec 31 T38N R15E; W2SW sec 14 T39N R13E and 2 lots in the platted town — lot 6 of block 4 in the town the register codes CHI (L6BL4CHI, as printed); lot 7 of block 4 in the town the register codes CHIV (L7BL4CHIV, as printed), 2428.28 acres stated in all, for $7629.82 (ls0617, ls0618, ls0628, ls0632, ls0633, ls0638, ls0639, ls0645, ls0652, ls0653, ls0662, ls0663, ls0670, ls0717, ls0730, ls0731, ls0732, ls0769, ls0770, ls0771, ls0796, ls0797, ls0950, ls0951, ls1234, ls1235). THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $4120.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: HUBBARD ELIJAH K matches Elijah Kent Hubbard: the forename names Elijah Kent Hubbard of the 5 people of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. what_it_supplies: A 665-roof production target with independently reconcilable group, district, level, and construction totals.
Thirty-five architectural family definitions with dimensional and massing bands.
District character, spacing, variation, finish, and chronology constraints for a July 1835 reconstruction.
A required distinction between named documentary landmarks and anonymous inferred infill.
what_it_does_not_supply: A surviving July 1835 building census or parcel-by-parcel roof register.
Exact locations, dimensions, appearance, occupants, or construction dates for anonymous roofs.
Authority to replace stronger building-specific evidence already represented in the dataset.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED / GENERATED, NOT AN ATTESTED NAMED BUILDING. The block, its scheduled roof count and its family mix follow the 665-roof programme; exact presence, lot, position, footprint, finish and instance-level form are interpretive.

fabric_basis.words: new-sawn clapboard on a balloon frame, 12-over-12 sash of 6 × 8 in glass and plain corner boards, under a new roof — a one-and-a-half-story cottage, new-built (rule F-T: a tradesman's by its type)

frontage.why: T-0105, the succession T-0079 owes: the core density standard applied to the next core block standing below the bar. THE FACE IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, by the command T-A14 made of it — tools/measure_street_frontage.py randolph washington market franklin — and on the committed dataset Randolph carries 7 documented records and 7 inferred households against Washington's 1 and 0. Randolph is this block's business face by the town's own record, so the block's one free lot on that face takes the row and both free lots on Washington stay open. THE END RULE IS T-A11'S, READ ON THIS BLOCK: this is the easternmost block the plat module reaches on the Randolph tier, so the town-centre end of its frontage is the WEST one, toward Dearborn Street and the only crossing of the main stem in July 1835 — and the row is graded that way, a storey and a half at the west end, a one-room frame cottage in the middle, and an older log cabin at the east. NO COORDINATE IS AUTHORED: the line, its bearing, the lot's own stretch of it and the end the run packs away from are all read from the committed block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and the 1.5 m setback is the plat module's own lot margin rather than a measurement of this frontage. Lot 4 is an interior lot and not a corner one, so the standard's third clause — a corner lot builds to the corner — has nothing to bind here; the run stands off both of its own side lines by that same margin.
